title: Garden District cocktail parties and Alcorn and French
summary: Playing cocktail parties for the St. Paul family, pay from wealthy patrons, and Alvin Alcorn and Albert French's character.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: No, no. Man, that guy was a saxophone player, a supreme. I mean, he, he gave the incentive to play. And I used to like to hire him. And sometimes I'd use, uh, Son Johnson, that's George Johnson, and Parnell together. Well, that's two of the best saxophone players in the city, see? And we had Al, Alvin Alcon, and Alvin French singing, and had a little fella called Jim Davis on the bass. But we had, I always did bring up there, a good outfit for those boys, and they were very well pleased, you see? And, uh, during the time I was playing like that, Miss Neda St. Paul, that was George St. Paul's daughter before she married. All her little cocktail parties she used to give on Phillip Street there. We played a couple of houses over there, too. Just the piano. And I went there a couple times by myself, so I thought I'd bring somebody to help me sing, so I brought Albert French. And we played about five or six parties for the St. Paul's. Well, that's in that, what they call the Garden District section. Yeah, pretty houses in there. Yeah. And, uh, they liked our music. They'd call me anytime, sometimes, nine or ten o'clock, asking where'd I come play for them. I told them, sure. And I'd just play the job around, and those people, that's one thing about those people, those kind of people, they would ask you how much you owe them. I'd always tell them, give me what they want, because I knew I'd be well paid, you know. Sometimes thirty dollars, sometimes forty dollars. People would just have the money to pay. They'd ask me if it was enough, because, you know, it was enough for three or four hours playing, see? So, we lost Albert. Papa Sellers, yeah. So, he would always throw jobs our way when Papa would have two jobs.

By the way, Alvin Alcorn is working with that group now again. Yeah, he is. They don't have Fernandes anymore. No. Albert's finances quit? Well, I don't know. There's some, maybe a disagreement or something, and so they're using Alvin at present. Well, I tell you. For some time now, a few weeks or months at least, here.

You know, he lives up on my rod, and I know he, I see him pretty often. I always see his family. He is a good trumpet player, yet. I mean, usually the trumpet players' lips go bad, you know. But he is a good trumpet player, and he's a nice fellow to be around. Some of the musicians, you don't care about being around, I have to admit. That's right. He's a wonderful fellow. He is a nice fellow. Albert French had one of the best dispositions for musicians. It's always a grill. He's always a grill. I mean, anywhere you'd go, we went to Biloxi with him, one of the Celestane's job, went to the Gulfport on Celestane's job with him. Celestane must have had two engagements that night, you know, so Albert would take the other one. But our kind of band we'd bring, honestly, I mean, it was a better band if it was the Papa than Celestane had, but people wanted Papa because of Papa. He had a big name, yeah. And we had better, yeah, we had Alvin Alcorn, guys like that, that's the girl, and he went away and he was playing with Kidora and those people.
Yeah, right. Went to Europe with him about two years, three years ago.
